question: A shopkeeper made a loss of ₹125 on an article. If the loss percentage was 5%, what was the cost price of the article (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In percentage terms, the Cost Price (CP) is always considered 100%.

The given loss is 5% of the Cost Price, which is equal to ₹125.

5% → ₹125

100% → (125 ÷ 5) × 100 = ₹2500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss incurred = ₹125

Loss percentage = 5%

 
 
 
• 
 Selling Price (95%)
 Loss (5%)
 

 Total Cost Price (100%)
 

 ₹125

**Formula Used:**

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ 5 = (125 ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ 5 × CP = 12500

⇒ CP = 12500 ÷ 5

⇒ CP = 2500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Base

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the base of Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise in the question.

Key Formulas

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

Selling Price (SP) Evaluation

When there is a profit: SP = CP × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100]
When there is a loss: SP = CP × [(100 − Loss %) ÷ 100]
